entries.title: John 12:1
segments:
Six days before the passover. On the eighth Nisan, after sunset and on the beginning of the Sabbath.  The Jewish day was reckoned from sunset to sunset.
 

 
Bethany. A village about two miles from Jerusalem, at the foot of the Mount of Olives.
 

 
Where Lazarus was. Added emphasis as to the truth of the resurrection of Lazarus, which had already been related in detail by the evangelist (

entries.title: John 12:2
segments: They made him a supper there. It was at the house of Simon the leper (

entries.title: John 12:3
segments:
A pound. Twelve ounces.
 

 
Nard. A fragrant ointment made from a kind of bearded grass found in India.

entries.title: John 12:5
segments: Three hundred shillings. About fifty dollars of our money.

entries.title: John 12:6
segments: The bag. In which the money needed by the apostles was carried.  Judas was the keeper or treasurer of this fund.  One bag or cash box for the whole community implies that no member of it had exclusive ownership of any part of the money.

entries.title: John 12:7
segments: Keep it against the day of my burying. That is, keep what is left for the anointing of my body on my burial day, which is near.

entries.title: John 12:10
segments: That they might put Lazarus also to death. They feared the effect of the miracle on the great mass of people.  Multitudes might acclaim Jesus both as political and religious leader.  Also the chief priests, most of whom were Sadducees, were angered by the thought of Lazarus raised from the dead, because denial of the resurrection was with them an important doctrine.

entries.title: John 12:11
segments: Went away, and believed on Jesus. Renounced Judaism and accepted Jesus as their Savior.

entries.title: John 12:12
segments:
:19
 
On the morrow a great multitude, etc.  The evangelist's account of the triumphal entry of Jesus into Jerusalem shows that inhabitants of the city as well as the great multitude of Galileans that had come to the feast, welcomed Jesus as the Messiah (
).  The 'morrow' of

was what is now called Palm Sunday.
 

 
Palm trees. Palm branches were commonly considered as symbols of triumph and rejoicing.  See notes on

entries.title: John 12:20
segments: Greeks. Gentiles.  They went up to worship at the feast, not because they were in full sympathy with the Jewish ritual, but by reason of their devout belief in one God.  They were 'proselytes of the gate,' not received into full membership in the Jewish community, but willing to accept some of its rules.

entries.title: John 12:22
segments: Philip. Both 'Philip' (lover of horses) and 'Andrew' (manly) were Greek names.  Both apostles were from Bethsaida, on the shore of the Sea of Galilee.

entries.title: John 12:23
segments: Should be glorified. By his suffering and death.

entries.title: John 12:24
segments: If it die, it beareth much fruit. Jesus, teaching these Gentiles, likens his coming crucifixion and its results to a process of nature.  As a grain of wheat can only impart its latent power of life and growth to the new plant by decaying and dying under the ground, so must the Son of man give up his human body to the operation of physical death, in order that his divine life and teaching may spring up into the bloom and fruitage of the Spirit for all mankind.

entries.title: John 12:25
segments: He that loveth his life loseth it. See notes on

entries.title: John 12:26
segments: Let him follow me. Jesus plainly tells the inquiring Gentiles that they too may hope to gain the larger life only by losing the smaller.  The life of worldly satisfaction and advantage must give way to the life of self-sacrifice, which they can know by following him.

entries.title: John 12:27
segments: Now is my soul troubled. The despair and anguish of his human nature.

entries.title: John 12:28
segments: Father, glorify thy name. By the passion, death and resurrection of Jesus.

entries.title: John 12:30
segments: For your sakes. That they might believe that Jesus came from God.

entries.title: John 12:31
segments:
The judgment of this world. The responsibility of accepting or rejecting Christ incurred by those who were soon to know of his death and resurrection.
 

 
The prince of this world. Satan.

entries.title: John 12:32
segments: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, etc.  Sympathy and love for an unselfish life and unselfish suffering, together with the hope of eternal life springing up in mankind as the result of a divine example of power over death, find their central attraction, their abiding assurance, in the Cross of Christ.

entries.title: John 12:35
segments: Jesus therefore said, etc.  He does not give the questioners a direct reply; but he merges all needless controversy in the affirmation that he is the light, and that they must believe in it and walk in it while they have it.  This was, in effect, telling him that he was the Messiah.

entries.title: John 12:36
segments: Hid himself. Most probably he went to Bethany.

entries.title: John 12:41
segments: His glory. The glory of Christ.

entries.title: John 12:42
segments: Even of the rulers many believed. Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea are the only known ones.  They did not openly profess their faith in Christ until after the crucifixion.

entries.title: John 12:44
segments:
:50
 
And Jesus cried and said, etc.  The words of Jesus contained in these verses are not a continuation of his last public discourse (
), but are recorded here for the purpose of strengthening what the evangelist had written about our Lord's life and work in

.
 

 
Believeth not on me, but on him that sent me Christ in these words about his person and mission directly declares that he came from the Father who sent him.
